promptState.text: A medium close-up photograph of a 27-year-old barista with short curly black hair, warm brown skin and a neat short beard, wearing a rust-orange canvas apron over a white t-shirt, standing behind a light oak cafe counter. With his right hand he pours steamed milk from a small steel jug into a white cappuccino cup that his left hand holds steady on the counter, a leaf of latte art forming in the foam. He looks down at the cup with a small, focused smile. Behind him, on a matte black wall, white hand-painted letters read "PIXA CAFE" above a shelf of glass jars of coffee beans and a few small potted plants. Clear morning sun from a window at camera-left lights his face and the steam rising from the cup, the right side of his face in soft shade. Shot at eye level with a 50mm lens at f/4, his face and the cup sharp, the wall a little soft. True-to-life colour, the fine grain of 35mm film.

MODELS AND NODES USED IN THIS WORKFLOW

 MOSS-Image needs ComfyUI 0.42.0 or newer, the first version with MOSS. On an older ComfyUI, Load CLIP has no moss_image type: update ComfyUI first.

 Load Diffusion Model

Download moss_image_sft_int8_convrot.safetensors5.41 GB  

Place in: ComfyUI/models/diffusion_models/moss

Create the moss folder if it does not exist.

Take the file with sft in its name: that is the finished model. The base files are the raw model, made for training LoRAs.

 Load CLIP

Download qwen3.5_9b_w4a8_gptq.safetensors7.34 GB  

Place in: ComfyUI/models/text_encoders

 Load VAE

Download flux2-vae_small.safetensors250 MB  

Place in: ComfyUI/models/vae

This is the small Flux 2 VAE, a different file from flux2-vae.safetensors.

 License

MOSS-Image is made by OpenMOSS and released under the Apache 2.0 license: you may use the pictures and the model commercially.

MOSS-Image model card 

 After placing the files, restart ComfyUI or refresh model lists using the R shortcut.

 Nodes Installed from Manager

  • Pixaroma: update to the latest version (these workflows need at least 1.4.214). A node shows red or missing? Update Pixaroma.

Which version is the newest? The Latest Pixaroma version button shows it and what is new in it. The help page has the update steps for every kind of install.

Latest Pixaroma version How to update Pixaroma 

 Something missing?

Each button opens a short video that shows the fix, with the steps written under it.

Red or missing nodes A model file is missing Buttons missing after an update 

 Resources

Join Discord  Pixaroma YouTube Channel  Ask for help

{"version":1,"content":"

HOW TO USE

The basic MOSS-Image workflow: write a prompt, press Run, get a picture. MOSS follows long, detailed prompts well and is very good at words in pictures.

 Steps

  1. Write your prompt in Prompt Pixaroma.
  2. Pick a size on Sizes Pixaroma.
  3. Leave the seed on F to repeat a picture, or switch it to R for a new one every Run.
  4. Press Run.

 Writing a prompt

  1. Start with the kind of picture: A close-up photograph of ..., A minimalist travel poster in flat screen-print style ..., Anime illustration ...
  2. Then the subject and what it does, the place, the light and where it comes from, and the camera: clear morning sun from camera-left, 50mm lens at f/4.
  3. Words that should appear go in double quotes: white hand-painted letters read "PIXA CAFE". For several lines, put each line in its own quotes on its own line, the way the menu in workflow 4 does.
  4. Skip 8k, masterpiece, best quality: describe what you want to SEE instead.

 MOSS also understands anime-style tag lists: best quality, highres, 1girl, solo, silver hair, cherry blossoms, smile. Plain sentences give more of the scene; tags give the classic anime look.

 More to try

The second example from the video: a 3D cartoon instead of a photo. Paste it into Prompt Pixaroma and press Run (size 1024 x 1280, seed 2):

Stylized 3D animated-film render with soft global illumination and a hand-sculpted, toy-like matte finish. A chubby young red panda with rusty orange and cream fur, an oversized round head, big dark glossy eyes with bright catchlights and a fluffy striped tail sits on a light oak kitchen counter, its cheeks stuffed full, holding a half-eaten chocolate chip cookie in both front paws close to its chest. Beside it a glass cookie jar lies tipped on its side with three cookies rolling out, and crumbs are scattered across the counter and on its belly fur. It looks straight at the camera with wide surprised eyes, caught in the act. Behind it a cozy kitchen with cream tiles and a small potted herb on the windowsill, softly out of focus. Warm evening light from a window at camera-left, a soft cool fill from the right. Medium shot at eye level with the counter, the red panda centered and sharp, a palette of rusty orange, cream, warm brown and soft sage green.

 Good to know

  • Words you did not ask for (a sign in the background, a poster on a wall) can come out as made-up letters. Give the words in quotes, or describe the thing as plain.
  • A short prompt works, but a long one gives you more control. Workflow 2 writes the long prompt for you from a short idea.
  • Want it faster? Workflow 3 makes the same kind of picture in about 1 second with a speed LoRA.

 Something not working?

Each button opens the answer on the Pixaroma help page.

Save to your own folder Nodes look different from the video 

","buttonColor":"#f66744","lineColor":"#f66744","backgroundColor":"#2a2a2a","info":{"title":"How to Use","icon":"to-do","color":"#2a9d8f"}}

{"version":1,"content":"

WHAT EACH NODE DOES

The colour of a node tells you what kind of node it is. Nothing here needs changing except the blue ones.

 Models to download

Orange. Each one needs a file from the Download Models note.

  • Load Diffusion Model (MOSS-Image SFT) - The image model, MOSS-Image SFT from OpenMOSS: a 5B text-to-image model that is very good at words in pictures and can follow a layout of boxes. The int8 file (5.4 GB) looks the same as the 10 GB bf16 file in our tests.
  • Load CLIP (Qwen 3.5 9B, reads the prompt) - Reads your prompt and turns the words into something MOSS understands. The type must be moss_image.
  • Load VAE (Flux 2 VAE small) - Turns the finished render into a picture. MOSS uses the small Flux 2 VAE, a different file from the normal flux2-vae.

 The steps you set

Blue, and numbered. These are the only nodes you need to touch.

  • Prompt Pixaroma (1. your prompt) - The prompt box. The demo prompt is a full description of the picture: write yours the same way (see How to Use).
  • Sizes Pixaroma (2. picture size) - The picture size. Click a size; the Portrait / Landscape switch turns it on its side. The demo is 1024 x 1280 (4:5). Full HD (1088 x 1920) and 2048 x 2048 give more detail and take longer (see Run Times): MOSS makes them in one go, with no doubled faces in our tests. Its latent output is the blank canvas MOSS paints on, straight into the KSampler (ComfyUI's own KSampler: a sampler from another node pack can make the picture twice too big).
  • Seed Pixaroma (3. fixed or random) - The seed. F (fixed) gives the same picture every Run, R (random) a new one each Run. The demo uses seed 2.

 The work

Green. They run by themselves.

  • CLIP Text Encode (reads the prompt) - Reads the prompt through the text encoder.
  • CLIP Text Encode (negative prompt) - The negative prompt from ComfyUI's own MOSS workflow and the MOSS user guide: nsfw, worst quality, bad anatomy, watermark, jpeg artifact. Leave it as it is.
  • Skip Layer Guidance (from ComfyUI's MOSS workflow) - A setting from ComfyUI's own MOSS workflow and the MOSS user guide: it skips layer 22 in the negative half of the first half of the steps. Leave it as it is.
  • KSampler (25 steps) - The render: 25 steps, CFG 2.5, er_sde, simple, the settings of ComfyUI's own MOSS workflow.
  • VAE Decode (latent to picture) - Turns the finished render into a picture.

 The result

Dark red, at the end.

  • Save Image Pixaroma (saves the picture) - Saves each picture as PNG into ComfyUI/output/MOSS Image and shows it on the node.

 Readouts

Dark. Nothing to set: they show you what happened.

  • Run Timer - The dark clock above the result shows how long the last Run took.

","buttonColor":"#f66744","lineColor":"#f66744","backgroundColor":"#2a2a2a","info":{"title":"Nodes Info","icon":"node-v5","color":"#3d7cc9"}}

widgets_values:
{"version":1,"content":"

RUN TIMES

Measured on a 24 GB RTX 4090 with this workflow, with the models already loaded. A different card gives different numbers, but the shape holds: the time grows with the number of pictures and their size.

SizeTime
1024 x 1024about 8 s
1024 x 1280 (the demo)about 9 s
Full HD, 1088 x 1920about 16 s
2048 x 2048about 41 s

 The first Run of the session

The first Run after starting ComfyUI also has to load the models from disk (MOSS and its text encoder, about 13 GB together), so it takes longer. After that they stay loaded.

","buttonColor":"#f66744","lineColor":"#f66744","backgroundColor":"#2a2a2a","info":{"title":"Run Times","icon":"run-timer","color":"#3f9a4f"}}
